articles.title: How to Use AI Tools Ethically While You Job Hunt
articles.excerpt: AI tools can make a job search less lonely and more organized. They can also make it easier to send a confident application that is not quite true, or to walk into an interview with answers you could…
articles.body: AI tools can make a job search less lonely and more organized. They can also make it easier to send a confident application that is not quite true, or to walk into an interview with answers you could not explain if someone asked a follow-up. The ethical line is not "never use a tool." It is simpler and stricter than that: the story you tell about your work has to be yours, and you have to be able to stand behind it in the room. Used well, AI is a drafting assistant, a research aide and a practice partner. Used poorly, it becomes a way to outsource the very judgment the employer is trying to hire. A practical standard: would you sign this, out loud?

articles.title: Raymarching a nebula: the basics, with an example shader
articles.excerpt: In an earlier devlog, we explained how we optimised the nebula of Vesper Protocol. Several readers asked us to start from the beginning. So here are the basics of volumetric raymarching, step by step,…
articles.body: In an earlier devlog, we explained how we optimised the nebula of Vesper Protocol. Several readers asked us to start from the beginning. So here are the basics of volumetric raymarching, step by step, with a complete GLSL shader you can paste into Shadertoy. The principle: stepping through a volume A typical game engine draws triangles: it projects their vertices onto the screen and colours the pixels they cover. That works very well for a spaceship or a wall. But a nebula has no surface: it is a cloud of gas, more or less dense, that light partly passes through. Raymarching flips the problem around. For each pixel, we cast a ray from the camera and walk along it in small steps.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989.
